newsitem.title: UK: Wolverhampton sees H2 margins improvement.
newsitem.headline: Wolverhampton sees H2 margins improvement.

text.p: Britain's Wolverhampton & Dudley Breweries Plc said on Wednesday it expected margins in the second half of the year to show a "substantial improvement".
However, the brewer said in a statement accompanying first half results it did not expect trading conditions to change significantly in the second half from the first half.

It said that expenditure on marketing and property refurbishment will not increase at the same rate as in the first half and added that the company will benefit from a 5p per pint increase that took effect on May 1.
Wolverhampton reported that first half pretax profits rose to 18.76 million stg compared with 18.18 previously. It raised its interim dividend payout to 6.6p per share from 6.0p.
The pretax profit result was near the top end of market expectations, helping shares in the company rise 6p to stand at 646-1/2p by 0826 GMT.

Turnover at the brewer rose 12.8 percent to 133.3 million stg during the first half. It said that it benefited from last year's investments in the expansion of its tied estate and greater distribution of its brands to wholesale customers.
"There was no evidence of a general improvement in retail trading conditions, with consumer confidence remaining fragile throughout the period," said chairman David Miller.
